question: Can even immense material wealth justify giving away the kaula teaching?
premises: An ocean filled with jewels represents immense wealth.
Such wealth may be accumulated by someone.
This is posed as a measure against giving the teaching.
inference: Even possession of an ocean full of jewels is not sufficient reason to disclose the teaching.
uncertainties: The form akretuṃ is obscure and may be corrupt or highly compressed.
plain_english: Even if one had an accumulation enough to fill the ocean with jewels.
